items.detail: grep -c 'OB1_REPO' docs/publish-transport.md -> 3 (was 0). Row at docs/publish-transport.md:52 inside the '## Operator configuration' table (line 41). The caveats paragraph at lines 60-66 gives OB1_REPO the same validation/interpolation treatment the table gives OB1_REMOTE_DIR: it names why OB1_REMOTE_DIR is validated (interpolated into the remote activation body, quotes/whitespace rejected, absolute required) and contrasts OB1_REPO — strictly local, not interpolated into the remote body so no remote-body validation of its own, while artifacts resolved from it must exist and be non-empty (exit 5), which matches require_artifacts at scripts/publish-catalog.sh:128-136.

items.criterion: Documented default matches the script's actual OB1_REPO fallback (parent of script dir) — doc claims what the code does
items.detail: docs/publish-transport.md:52 says 'parent of the checkout's `scripts/` dir'; scripts/publish-catalog.sh:71 resolves `REPO="${OB1_REPO:-$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)}"` (i.e., parent of the script's directory). Identical semantics, no drift between doc and code. scripts/ob1-distribute.sh:38 has a different fallback ($HOME/off-by-one) but the criterion scopes the row to the publish-catalog default and the row is not contradicted for that script.

items.criterion: The caveats paragraph's exit-5 claims are true in code: OB1_REPO-derived artifacts must exist and be non-empty, OB1_REPO itself is not validated/interpolated remotely
items.detail: scripts/publish-catalog.sh:128-136 (require_artifacts): `[ ! -s "$BINARY" ]` and `[ ! -s "$DB" ]` each `return "$EXIT_CONFIG"` (=5, defined line 55) — matches 'must exist and be non-empty (exit 5)'. items.detail: Ran `make transport-retry-selftest` fresh this session: exit_code 0, decisive output 'transport-retry self-test: 108/108 checks passed — ALL GREEN'.
